LESSON: READING 2.2.1 INTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: FAMILY CELEBRATIONS SUGGESTED VOCABULARY: celebrate, ribbon, ceremony, invitatio
Topic 2.2: Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading, part of FAMILY CELEBRATIONS SUGGESTED VOCABULARY: celebrate, ribbon, ceremony, invitatio in Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why should we read the title and pictures in a story? 2. What is your favourite poem or story?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. read poems or stories related to the theme for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. apply appropriate reading techniques to answer direct and indirect questions based on a poem or story for self- expression,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. realise the importance of reading comprehension for lifelong learning.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. read poems or stories related to the theme for comprehension,

   Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. apply appropriate reading techniques to answer direct and indirect questions based on a poem or story for self- expression,

   Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. realise the importance of reading comprehension for lifelong learning.

   Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. talk about pictures and the title of a poem and story (featuring similes and sayings) together,

2. read a poem or story (featuring similes and sayings) in print and non-print texts related to the theme for comprehension,

3. identify events in a poem or a story for logical and fluent flow,

4. find new words and similes in a poem or story with peers,

5. recite the poem and answer oral questions from poems and stories (featuring similes and sayings),

6. participate in a readers’ theatre collaboratively to read a story,

7. discuss and role-play events in a text based on the theme,

8. watch a video related to the theme for specific information. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. talk about pictures and the title of a poem and story (featuring similes and sayings) together,
2. read a poem or story (featuring similes and sayings) in print and non-print texts related to the theme for comprehension,
3. identify events in a poem or a story for logical and fluent flow,
4. find new words and similes in a poem or story with peers,
5. recite the poem and answer oral questions from poems and stories (featuring similes and sayings),
6. participate in a readers’ theatre collaboratively to read a story,
7. discuss and role-play events in a text based on the theme,
8. watch a video related to the theme for specific information. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy: This is developed as the learner is able to identify and talk about events in a story logically and fluently.

• Learning to learn: It is enhanced as the learner uses appropriate reading techniques to answer questions appropriately.

Values:
● Social justice: This is promoted as the learner fosters fairness by allowing equal opportunities to peers when

participating in a readers' theatre.

• Responsibility: This is enhanced as the learner engages in assigned roles and duties diligently.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Self-esteem: It is developed as the learner gains confidence as they recite poems or stories with peers.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to link the concept of reading poems and songs to their learning in Creative Arts.
